A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CROPI research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLVR training experiments, mathematical reasoning benchmark results, timing measurements, and analyses of gradient estimation and selected data.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds convergence, fixed-time, random-selection, and rollout-cost comparisons.

M1.justification: Off-policy gradient estimation, sparse projection, cosine-based influence, reciprocal-rank fusion, and phase-wise GRPO selection remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. The refreshed 10% subset explanation clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same mathematical reasoning training data and six evaluation benchmarks. The additions investigate retained coverage through different budgets and controls, without introducing another dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix E.5 adds a phase-wise random 10% selection comparator, evaluated against CROPI and full-data GRPO in Table 5. The original Learnability, Pass Rate, Influence Function, DAPO, and full-data comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds a stated 2,000-step peak-accuracy comparison, fixed 12/18/24-hour evaluations, and random selection under CROPI's retained schedule. The new rollout-cost test matches batch size 128 and an 8,192-token cap across operations. These are supplementary protocols; the original main experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices E.4–E.5 and F add focused checks of longer-run convergence, wall-clock efficiency, whether random subsampling explains the gains, and rollout versus gradient-computation cost. Existing gradient-fidelity, projection, and selected-data analyses are retained under shifted appendix labels.

E5.justification: v2 first explicitly documents five-point moving averages for reported Acc.@step values and training curves, including Table 1 and Figure 3. This clarifies statistical aggregation of existing results; it does not establish additional runs. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 values and plotted results are unchanged. New Tables 3–5 and 8 report CROPI/GRPO peak accuracies of 71.05%/70.17%, fixed-time accuracies, random-selection scores of 67.29%/68.04% at 500/1,000 steps, and rollout/forward-backward times of 319.80/35.91 seconds. Section 5.2 additionally reports a direct 2.17× time-to-70%-accuracy speedup. These are supplementary results, not revised same-setting benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The influence definitions, off-policy approximations, assumptions, and derivations in Appendices A–B remain mathematically unchanged. The revised sentence introducing token-level importance sampling is a grammatical repair.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scope: rollout-free influence estimation, sparse gradient projection, and CROPI's training efficiency, including the 2.66× step-level acceleration claim. New experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the random-selection control as evidence that gains do not arise simply from reducing training-set size. Section 3 and Appendix F also add a hardware explanation contrasting compute-bound forward/backward computation with memory-bandwidth-constrained decoding. Existing limitations and other interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a CROPI code-access link. v2 also documents the smoothing window and conditions for the new timing comparison. Original prompt templates, training hyperparameters, frameworks, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked code's contents.

R1.justification: Appendix C.2 now acknowledges Hu et al. (2025)'s promising empirical results and replaces the characterization of its objective as 'largely heuristic' with a distinction between training objectives. The cited-work set otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, including RLVF to RLVR, clarifies selection and reporting descriptions, and inserts experimental subsections plus a rollout-cost appendix. The main narrative structure and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact tables, renumbers the existing appendix tables, expands smoothing-related captions, and reflows figures and text. All 18 figures are retained without changed graphic content, and the overall document design remains the same.

improvement.justification: The random-selection control and direct convergence/time comparisons strengthen evidence for CROPI's existing efficiency claims, while smoothing disclosure and the code pointer improve transparency. These gains are focused on the 1.5B setting and lack added uncertainty across training runs. The unchanged limitation describing fewer than 1,000 training steps also conflicts with the new 2,000-step study. Overall, the added evidence provides a limited, clear quality improvement.
